agricultural: broad cultivated land with regular field texture and open farmland layout, distinguishing agricultural from golfcourse by lacking manicured fairway patterns and from chaparral by lacking dense dry shrub texture.
airplane: visible aircraft body with wings and tail, compact object-level structure, and clear airplane contours, distinguishing airplane from runway which appears as a long straight paved strip without a discrete fuselage.
baseballdiamond: compact sports field with a distinct diamond-shaped infield, distinguishing baseballdiamond from tenniscourt by lacking multiple narrow rectangular courts and fence-aligned court markings.
beach: bright shoreline region with a clear sand-water boundary, distinguishing beach from harbor by lacking dense dock infrastructure and from chaparral by lacking dry shrub-covered terrain.
buildings: large roofed man-made structures with block-like geometry and organized built-up layout, distinguishing buildings from denseresidential by stronger individual roof mass, from parkinglot by having dominant building footprints rather than open paved space, and from mobilehomepark by lacking repetitive trailer-like rows.
chaparral: irregular dry shrub-covered terrain with coarse natural texture and sparse woody vegetation, distinguishing chaparral from agricultural by lacking regular cultivated parcels, from beach by lacking a sand-water shoreline, and from sparseresidential by lacking repeated residential roof patterns.
denseresidential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing, distinguishing denseresidential from mobilehomepark by less uniform trailer-row organization, from buildings by smaller and more repetitive housing roofs, and from sparseresidential by much closer building intervals.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with natural dark-green texture, distinguishing forest from agricultural by lacking regular field boundaries and cultivated parcel structure.
freeway: wide multi-lane transportation corridor with continuous road surface and branching traffic structure, distinguishing freeway from overpass by emphasizing extended horizontal road flow, from runway by lacking aviation strip markings, and from storagetanks by lacking compact circular industrial containers.
golfcourse: well-maintained green fairways with landscaped grass regions and designed open-course layout, distinguishing golfcourse from agricultural by lacking regular crop parcels and from chaparral by lacking dry shrub texture.
harbor: waterfront port area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent infrastructure, distinguishing harbor from parkinglot by the presence of water and port-side organization, from storagetanks by stronger dock-water context, and from beach by denser man-made coastal infrastructure.
intersection: road crossing region where multiple transportation lines meet, distinguishing intersection from denseresidential by road-dominant junction geometry, from river by lacking a continuous natural water channel, and from freeway by emphasizing a crossing node rather than an extended corridor.
mediumresidential: moderately spaced residential buildings with visible yards and balanced housing density, distinguishing mediumresidential from denseresidential by larger spacing, from mobilehomepark by less uniform trailer-row structure, and from buildings by a more residential neighborhood layout.
mobilehomepark: repetitive small elongated housing units arranged in orderly rows, distinguishing mobilehomepark from denseresidential by its more regular trailer-like layout, from buildings by much smaller residential units, and from tenniscourt by lacking court markings and sports geometry.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation, distinguishing overpass from freeway by its crossing and bridge-like form and from runway by lacking a long flat aviation strip.
parkinglot: large open paved area with organized parking spaces and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parkinglot from harbor by lacking water and dock structures and from buildings by lacking dominant roofed structures.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous channel shape and visible banks, distinguishing river from intersection by lacking road-junction geometry and from chaparral by having clear water appearance rather than dry shrub texture.
runway: long straight paved strip with elongated linear geometry and open surroundings, distinguishing runway from airplane by lacking a discrete aircraft body, from freeway by lacking complex road-network branching, and from overpass by lacking elevated crossing structure.
sparseresidential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density, distinguishing sparseresidential from denseresidential by much larger spacing, from mobilehomepark by lacking regular trailer rows, and from chaparral by showing repeated roof structures instead of natural shrub texture.
storagetanks: large circular or cylindrical industrial containers with highly regular round geometry, distinguishing storagetanks from freeway by lacking long road corridors and from harbor by emphasizing clustered tank shapes rather than dock-water layout.
tenniscourt: small rectangular court surfaces with clear line markings and repeated sports-court geometry, distinguishing tenniscourt from denseresidential by lacking residential roof clusters, from mobilehomepark by lacking trailer-like housing rows, and from baseballdiamond by lacking a diamond-shaped infield.
